Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Chinese President Xi Jinping shake hands after a bilateral meeting Tuesday in Shenzhen, China. Credit: Mark Carney via X.
By: Northern Miner Staff November 17, 2026
Canada will expand tariff relief on Chinese steel and aluminum products in short supply at home and extend existing exemptions through 2028, as Prime Minister Mark Carney broadens a trade accord with Beijing.
The expansion covers all or part of 23 steel and nine aluminum tariff items for which Canadian supply is insufficient or unavailable, Canada’s federal government said Tuesday after Carney met President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen. In exchange, China will provide additional tariff relief on about $400 million (US$280 million) in Canadian pork, fish and seafood exports.
“Canada and China have recalibrated our relationship to the benefit of citizens in both countries,” Carney said in a statement.
The agreement announced Tuesday eases import costs for Canadian manufacturers that cannot source enough of the specified metals domestically, while preserving the wider tariff framework intended to protect Canadian production. Ottawa’s broader duties on Chinese steel and aluminum remain in place.
U.S. demand
U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer warned in an Aug. 26 CBC interview that tariff relief for Canadian steel and aluminum would require safeguards against foreign metals entering the American market through Canada. Washington wanted Ottawa to align its trade protections to prevent that route, he said.
The White House’s Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy named Canada among China’s “biggest enablers” in an August assessment of tariff evasion. Chinese exporters were routing goods through third countries and misrepresenting their origin to obtain lower U.S. duties, the office alleged.
Canada imposed a 25% surtax on specified Chinese steel and aluminum imports in October 2024, citing non-market policies and practices that threatened domestic production and investment. The measure remains part of Ottawa’s metals tariff system, alongside separate rules covering steel import quotas and goods containing metal originally made in China. The exemptions, known as remissions, relieve importers of duties on qualifying products. Existing product-specific relief applies to all importers of the listed goods, while businesses whose products are not covered can request exceptional relief, the Department of Finance says.
January accord
The latest measures build on the countries’ January trade arrangement. Earlier relief covered 66 lines of product-specific remissions and 49 tariff lines of company-specific remissions. Ottawa also added coverage for seven steel, two aluminum and four steel derivative products under that arrangement, Global Affairs Canada said in a background document . The new two-year extension moves the expiry of existing metals relief from the end of 2026 to the end of 2028. Ottawa tied the additional 32 tariff items to gaps in Canadian supply. The leaders’ announcement didn’t identify individual manufacturers that would benefit. The broader thaw also affects the battery supply chain. Canada’s January arrangement with China set an initial quota for 49,000 Chinese electric vehicles at a 6.1% tariff. About 16,200 vehicles have entered Canada under the arrangement since March, Global Affairs Canada said. Separately, Carney said Canada would conduct a trade mission to China in 2027. The renewed relationship has restored access for more than 90% of Canadian trade previously affected by tariff action, representing nearly $7.5 billion in exports, Ottawa says.

Ford Police Interceptor Utility Recalled Over Map Lights That Refuse To Turn Off
7 photos
Photo: Ford
Clearly derived from the civilian-spec Explorer, the Police Interceptor Utility has been hit with a recall over a rather strange electrical issue. As it happens, a startup diagnostic may switch on both front map lights. Not a biggie per se, but the problem here is that said startup diagnostic may also leave the overhead console unable to turn those map lights off.
Ford is recalling an estimated 33,578 examples of the Police Interceptor Utility to fix this concern, a condition that violates federal lighting requirements. According to the Dearborn-based automaker, the power distribution box performs a diagnostic check at startup. The check briefly raises voltage on the interior lighting circuit, and the overhead console may not finish initializing all of its electronics when this happens.
The microcontroller, therefore, could mistake the electrical signal for a 'Global On' command. Dealer software and third-party tools are used by service technicians to trigger this command in order to verify that the body control module is properly sending power and signals to all interior lights, making it easier than pressing all interior light switches.
Ford explains in the recall documentation that the individual buttons for the front map lights become ineffective, leaving the driver and front passenger unable to switch off said lights. 26V726 is what the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration calls this campaign, with 26C50 being the automaker's number for it. Production dates for the affected vehicle population range from March 3, 2025, through October 23, 2026.
This also means that both 2026 and 2027 models are being recalled. Because the Police Interceptor Utility features unique overhead console hardware and software, this campaign doesn't include the Explorer. As for the regulatory issue, Ford points the finger at FMVSS 101.
Photo: Ford Pro Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 101 governs controls and displays, and section S5.3.4(a) requires a means to switch off any source of illumination in the front row. The phantom 'Global On' command makes those switches ineffective, creating a noncompliance condition. And yes, section S5.3.4(a) understandably requires all controls to perform their intended function.
As for the safety risks associated with driving with the map lights on, interior glare comes to mind. The Chicago Assembly Plant Vehicle Team identified this problem in June 2026, and the automaker's Critical Concern Review Group immediately opened an investigation. In the first instance, the safety boffins concluded that the issue would not develop while driving.
Curiously enough, Ford also decided that the condition did not constitute regulatory noncompliance. That interpretation would be proved wrong in August 2026, when Ford started discussing the problem with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. Worse still, Ford became aware of 69 warranty claims in the US market by the end of October 13, 2026.
The fix depends on the console's production date. Dealers will replace overhead consoles in vehicles produced before July 9, 2026, while those from July 10 through October 23 will be inspected for an SW2 marking. Any console that carries the marking in question will be reinstalled at no charge to affected law enforcement, government agencies, and other customers.

Loftware agreed to buy Seagull Software, the maker of BarTender, a labeling and tracking platform used by more than 250,000 organizations. The deal would bring BarTender’s barcode printing and item-level tracking tools into the same business as Loftware’s packaging artwork and supplier labeling software .
What’s Related
Loftware, based in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, said the combined business would cover more of the work involved in identifying a product, from designing its packaging to printing its label and tracking it through the supply chain.
Seagull, based in Redmond, Washington, makes software that automates the design and printing of labels, barcodes, and radio-frequency identification ( RFID ) tags. Seagull says customers use BarTender to handle more than 100 billion labels, tags, date codes and other identifiers each year.
Tracking starts when a label prints
In May, Seagull connected BarTender’s labeling software to its Track & Trace product. When a label prints, the software can automatically register the item for tracking and pass along details such as the item’s unique code, the time of printing, and its location. That saves workers from entering the same information into a tracking system by hand.
BarTender can also exchange data with warehouse management and enterprise planning systems. A warehouse can use that connection to check whether outbound shipments match the quantities on a shipping order or pull current inventory data for a cycle count. Seagull added to its item-tracking business in 2024 when it combined with inventory software company Mojix.
RELATED: Loftware Buys BL.INK to Boost QR Codes and Product Tracking
How Loftware handles supplier labels
Loftware’s software helps companies manage labels for large product catalogs across multiple sites. Its Smartflow product handles packaging artwork reviews and approvals. In April, the company launched Loftware Connect, which lets a buyer publish labeling requirements and lets approved suppliers use those requirements to label shipments without accessing the buyer’s internal systems.
Still waiting on timeline
The agreement follows Loftware’s 2021 combination with NiceLabel, another label design and printing software company. That deal brought NiceLabel under Loftware’s corporate brand while keeping the NiceLabel name on its products. The Seagull agreement would put NiceLabel and BarTender under the same owner.
Loftware said it expects customers to be able to keep using their existing systems as the companies come together. The announcement gave no timeline for connecting the products and provided no details on future licensing or pricing for BarTender customers.

Ford Drops New 2028 Mustang GTD 1901, It’s a Special Edition That Honors the Past
11 photos
Photo: Ford
It’s been more than three years since Ford pulled the wraps off the Mustang GTD , a street-version of its GT3 racer that was introduced for the 2025 model year, with a suffix that stands for Grand Touring Daytona, and the company now has a new special edition version of this model.
Nope, it’s not the GTD Competition, which managed to lap the Nurburgring in an impressive 6:40.835 earlier this year, boasting revised aerodynamics, fresh rubber, some weight-saving measures and more oomph over the regular GTD, but something that looks at the past. It’s called the GTD 1901, and it is an homage to Henry Ford’s first racer.
The Blue Oval hadn’t yet been founded when Henry Ford built the 26-horsepower, 8.8-liter, two-cylinder race car called the Sweepstakes. He put it through its paces on a dirt track outside Detroit, and since he was pretty much a raw novice, the odds were against him. However, in the end, he won the race, and took home a $1,000 cash prize, which is roughly $40,000 today, as well as a glass punch bowl, and made a name for himself.
A Scientific American article noted that the racer “ possesses features entitling it to credit as being the most unconventional, if not the most beautiful, design so far produced by American ingenuity. ” The recognition and credibility from that historic race allowed Henry Ford to secure the financing needed to start his second company (after the Detroit Automobile Company in 1900), and that is Ford Motor Company, which still exists today.
Photo: Ford Ford’s new Mustang GTD 1901 is a 2028 model year car, and pretty much a livery package that follows in the footsteps of the GTD Spirit of America. It replaces the latter, and just like it, it benefits from the Performance Package, which is standard. This includes underbody flaps, a unique face with dive planes, an active rear wing, a bigger splitter attached to the front bumper, and less sound deadening.
The chin spoiler, rocker, diffuser, and wing have exposed carbon fiber accents on them, and besides these, the new model also debuts the magnesium wheels, which are available, and reduce the car’s weight by 50.3 pounds (22.8 kg), according to the automaker. A new painted racing stripe option has also been added to the Mustang GTD, thus enhancing the customization choices available for this model.
By the way, the available magnesium wheels were supposed to be offered on the regular GTD when it launched for the 2025 model year, but they ended up being delayed. These wheels will also be available on the non-1901 versions of the GTD in black or luster nickel, and the Blue Oval is considering launching them as a retrofit option for current GTD owners who want to upgrade their rides.
Painted stripes instead of decals are another novelty, and the rare and eye-wateringly expensive muscle car also benefits from full-grain leather trim on the center console, dashboard panel, and door cards when it comes to the new Ford Mustang GTD 1901. The gear selector dial and the titanium paddle shifters, with the latter being part of the optional titanium trim package, have also been redesigned.
Beneath the skin lies the same Multimatic suspension with inboard springs and dampers at the rear, which can be watched through a dedicated window inside, and the model also benefits from the familiar supercharged V8, making 815 horsepower, and an eight-speed dual-clutch transmission.
Photo: Ford Details surrounding the pricing and availability of the new Ford Mustang GTD 1901 haven’t yet been disclosed, though the company noted that around 20 percent of the total production will comprise the 1901 model. Deliveries are scheduled to commence in the second quarter of 2027, and the Benjamins haven’t been mentioned. Nevertheless, interested parties should expect to pay over $400,000 for such a thing, which is pretty much new-gen supercar money.
Would you add a 1901 version of the Ford Mustang GTD to your collection if money were the least of your concerns? What about a regular GTD? Or would you perhaps wait for the brand to drop the new Mustang GTD Competition, with its unspecified power increase, and other changes?
You should know that for roughly $400K, your could buy a new supercar, like the Lamborghini Temerario, which has 907 horsepower (920 ps/677 kW) available via the right pedal. That’s how much the plug-in hybrid 4-liter twin-turbo V8 develops in total, enabling a 213 mph (343 kph) top speed, and 0-62 mph (0-97 kph) in 2.7 seconds.
There is also a Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC on sale, which kicks off at $106,090 (MSRP), and features a supercharged 5.2-liter V8 engine rated at 795 hp (806 ps/593 kW). But is the Mustang GTD (1901) roughly four times the car? You be the judge of that, and don’t forget to drop a few lines below to reveal your impression on this new 2028 MY muscle car.

BMW's M4 Convertible Getting a Battery-Electric Neue Klasse Makeover, New Model Spied in a Premiere
20 photos
Photo: SH Proshots
A few hours ago, we wrote about the upcoming BMW M3 Electric , which was just caught in the open flaunting its trippy camouflage and its Neue Klasse design, and now it is time for its open-top sibling to sit under the spotlight.
We are talking about the BMW M4 Convertible’s entirely-new generation, although it is unrelated to the G5X 3 Series, which is based on an updated version of the CLAR platform, as it’s the cabrio version of the latest i3. This means that it packs battery-electric firepower, and it utilizes the same Neue Klasse NAx construction.
Therefore, instead of sharing its nuts and bolts with the upcoming BMW M3, it will have numerous things in common with the first-ever M3 Electric . And this includes the quad-motor setup providing the firepower. We still do not know how much oomph it has, as while some say that it could have either 700 or maybe 800 horsepower, others are convinced that it could boast around 1,000 horsepower.
The latest information coming from the automotive world suggests that an estimated 850 horsepower could be the combined output of the BMW M3 Electric, and if that is indeed the case, then we don’t see why the M4 Convertible Electric won’t have that much oomph available via the right pedal. The output is in metric horsepower, and 850 ps translates to 838 brake horsepower and 625 kilowatts.
Photo: SH Proshots According to the rumor mill, the zero-emission M3 should weight in the region of 2.3 metric tons. That’s over 5,000 pounds. This likely means that all-quiet M4 Convertible will be even heavier. It should share the same battery pack with its four-door sibling, which is understood to have a 100 kWh or so capacity, presumably enabling a WLTP range of around 650 kilometers, or 400+ miles. The battery can be reportedly charged at up to 420 kW, and plugging it in might add up to 350 km (217 miles) of range in approximately ten minutes.
This scooped BMW M4 Convertible Electric is a prototype, albeit an early one, which is why some panels do not properly align. We were tempted to say that it is a mule, but we can clearly see that all body panels are new, and it looks nothing like the current ICE-powered open-top BMW M4. It features the same front fascia as the upcoming M3 Electric, and the front and rear bumpers should also look the same.
These will be inspired by the ones of the BMW M Concept Neue Klasse from earlier this year. Don’t mind the taillights on this scooped tester, because these are provisional. The final ones will likely be identical to those featured on the zero-emission M3. The model sports power-folding rag top that stows away behind a special compartment behind the seats, just like in the current M4 Convertible.
Photo: SH Proshots Some will argue that a folding hardtop would have been better, but a soft top not only helps keep the weight in check (well, as much as it can, because this is still a heavy EV), but also lowers the center of gravity, thus enabling faster cornering credentials. And that’s exactly what it needs if the open-top, zero-emission BMW M4 wants to attract real petrolheads.
While the cabin has yet to open up to the camera, we already know what it will look like. That’s because it is the same Neue Klasse setup as seen on other modern-day Bimmers . Thus, expect the same free-floating infotainment screen, dashboard panel, air vents, and the Panoramic iDrive stretching from one pillar to the other at the bottom of the windscreen. The steering wheel, special trim and upholstery, and other M-infused elements will obviously be shared with the upcoming BMW M3 Electric.
It will be interesting to see how the first-ever battery-electric BMW M4 Convertible feels and drives in the real world, and if it is anything as exciting as the current M4 Competition xDrive Convertible. The latter has 523 hp (530 ps/390 kW) to play with from its familiar 3.0-liter TwinPower Turbo straight-six engine, taking 3.6 seconds from 0-60 mph (0-97 kph). It is two-tenths of a second slower than the M4 Competition xDrive Coupe for those keeping track of the numbers.
Pricing for the outgoing BMW M4 Competition xDrive Convertible starts at $98,400 in the United States of America, whereas its fixed-roof sibling has an MSRP of $91,500. The lesser M4 Competition Coupe and the base M4 Coupe kick off at $86,400 and $82,200, respectively, and while the former has 503 hp (510 ps/375 kW), the latter comes with 473 hp (480 ps/353 kW)., enabling 0-60 mph in 3.8 and 4.1 seconds, respectively.
BMW’s first-ever M3 Electric is understood to launch sometime in 2027, and chances are that the M4 Convertible Electric might follow roughly one year later. The next-gen ICE-powered BMW M3 is also expected to premiere in 2028.

Khorfakkan
By Angelo Mathais India correspondent
17 November 2026
Apart from the lingering pressure of ocean freight rates that remain stubbornly elevated, India-Middle East shippers are facing various extra cost shocks, due to shifting carriers’ cargo handling policies and landside supply chain hurdles in the conflict region.
According to industry sources, fresh booking curbs imposed by mainline operators like Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd have further constrained capacity options for India’s cargo flows to the Persian Gulf.
With available vessel space from JNPA (Nhava Sheva) and Mundra to Khor Fakkan and Fujairah in the UAE, and Sohar in Oman, becoming tighter and more erratic, rates for these “lifeline” port pairs have risen from the levels seen last month, data suggests.
Spot rates offered by CMA CGM for JNPA to Khor Fakkan are around $7,500 per 40ft, compared with $6,500 to $7,000 in the second half of October.
Among the mainliners, CMA CGM has most sailings from India to the Persian Gulf via its Bigex network, as the carrier expanded Red Sea operations in a strategic approach. NVOs had traditionally dominated India-Middle East trade through slot deals with the mainline carriers.
“We do not expect any sort of rate relief in the near term,” one forwarder source told The Loadstar . “With fewer sailings, active capacity providers have the room to adjust rates dynamically.”
Rates ex-India to the other Gulf ports of discharge have also climbed month on month because of the supply-side issues, sources said.
CMA CGM’s spot rates for a 40ft booking from JNPA to Sohar are around $6,500, nearly double what the carrier was quoting at the end of September.
And the Gulf trade pain for shippers goes beyond soaring ocean rates. Hefty carrier charges linked to empty container drop-off at the destination are another significant cost. For example, Maersk is now charging as much as $1,200 per 40ft container for returns to the Sajaa dry port in the UAE, its designated yard for imports via Khor Fakkan. Sajaa, operated by Gulftainer, is roughly 90km from Khor Fakkan.
Maersk warned customers this week: “Vessel congestion and limited berthing availability at Khor Fakkan, together with high yard utilisation, road congestion and extended truck waiting times, are delaying cargo clearance.
“These conditions may affect import and export movements, including bonded transport to and from Ajman, Jebel Ali and other destinations.”
Similarly, Hapag-Lloyd, in a fresh Middle East operational update, has asked customers to confirm their preferred customs clearance or delivery location for UAE-bound imports by today, pushing them to pick up containers directly from the Sajaa depot, but also permitting collection at Khorfakkan, subject to requirements.
Customers who provide no instructions will have their cargo routed through Sajaa. The carrier said Sajaa offered 12 days of terminal free time and lower destination land freight charges.
UAE importers failing to notify the delivery instructions may run the risk of delayed customs clearance and additional storage/demurrage charges, in addition to container transfers imposed by Khor Fakkan terminal operators, sources said.

CPC Fleet Solutions used to spend one to two months finding a single drop yard for its private fleets. Through Truck Parking Club’s Fleet Parking service, it secured seven yards for 47 power units and more than 120 trailers in two months, Truck Parking Club said in a Nov. 12 release.
For a fleet that hauls for shippers, yard space can decide whether a new lane happens at all. Truck Parking Club already lets fleets book five or more truck and trailer spaces as a single account . Its Fleet Parking team takes on the legwork: a dedicated specialist finds the yards, works with the property owners and puts every site on one account and one monthly invoice.
The search often starts when a shipper awards a new lane, said Reed Loustalot, Truck Parking Club’s chief marketing officer.
“If you get a new lane from a shipper and it requires drop trailers and there’s nowhere at their DC for them to store them, you’ve got to go find a piece of property,” Loustalot told FreightWaves. “It’s going to take you some time, and sales might be waiting on an okay that we can do the business.”
How CPC found yards before
Based in Chesterfield, Missouri, CPC Logistics was founded in 1973 . It runs private fleets for shippers across North America through CPC Fleet Solutions, according to the release.
Those fleets need domicile yards for specific clients and drop yards at relay points, said Nick Sablich, a regional manager at CPC Fleet Solutions. Finding each one fell to CPC managers, who looked at properties, negotiated and went “back and forth to legal, making sure all the red lines are met,” he said.
“To go find a yard the old way, it was taking at least a month or two months, even more,” he said in the release. “Having you guys as the liaison to talk to the property owners saved me about 10 years of my life.”
What the Fleet Parking specialist does
Working with Truck Parking Club’s Fleet Parking Team, a fleet tells its dedicated specialist where it needs space, how many trucks and trailers it has to park and for how long. It also lists what the site must have, such as cameras, gated access or fencing. The specialist then searches more than 7,600 locations, plus a broader network of private, fleet-only sites, to find the best, most efficient location for those requirements. If nothing in the network fits, the team sources a new yard.
A fleet “can send us an address and be like, ‘Hey, we need 25 spaces within five miles of here, and they need these amenities,'” Loustalot said. In his example, that meant a fence, gate, lights and 24/7 access.
Every yard sits under one Truck Parking Club account, and each location can carry the fleet’s cost code. That removes the site visits, cold calls, checks and one-off legal agreements a fleet would otherwise handle for every new yard, Loustalot said.
“Freight moves faster than real estate,” Kaleb Knipp, vice president of Fleet Parking at Truck Parking Club, said in the release. “A new lane or a lost yard should not take two months to solve.”
CPC tests yards before committing
The release says CPC started with three yards in August and moved all three to one-year agreements in September. It now has yards in five states, with more under review.
Sablich called trying a site first one of the best things CPC could do. A location “might look great on the map, but it might not work,” he said.
“Down towards Atlanta, the traffic is real tough in those areas. Or if you’re up in the mountains, the grade that you have to go on up the mountain, it could slow down hours of service , how many gate houses they have to go through,” he said. “Sometimes if you try it to see how it works first, you get a better plan of operationally how you can make it work.”
Overflow space for shippers
The yards also cover lanes where CPC has nowhere to leave trailers.
“It comes down to drop rights,” Sablich said. “If we start up a new lane and we don’t have the drop rights and we need to move trailers somewhere, we have that option now to do that.”
When a client’s own lot fills up, CPC can have Truck Parking Club book an overflow yard for a month, he said. Peak season brings another use: shippers doing inventory hold on to trailers and need more before they can unload. Being able to offer staging options in those areas has “expanded our portfolio to help out with our clients,” Sablich said.
“Our time is money, and we have saved thousands of hours doing it this way,” he said.
Loustalot said Truck Parking Club plans to keep adding locations, with a focus on getting denser in high-demand markets. “Every single location we add is a new option for a fleet to service customers in new ways,” he said.
Why it matters: Dedicated and private fleet operators quoting new shipper lanes can line up drop yards without a months-long search and put manager time back on running the fleet.

Amazon officially opened its first Puerto Rico delivery station on Nov. 16 in Dorado. The company says customers across the San Juan metro area can now receive packages in about two days, compared with waits of up to two weeks before the station began making deliveries.
What’s Related
The 100,000-square-foot station began delivering packages in August, three months before the formal opening. It’s Amazon’s first logistics facility in the Caribbean. Puerto Rico Gov. Jenniffer González-Colón and Dorado Mayor Aníbal José Torres attended the opening.
The station employs more than 100 people, and six independent delivery companies based there account for about 300 additional driver roles, Amazon said. Hiring is still underway ahead of the holiday shopping season .
RELATED: Ranking the Top 50 Global Third-Party Logistics Providers
How packages move through Dorado
The Dorado station handles the last step before packages reach customers. Workers receive incoming parcels, sort them by delivery route, and load them into vans. Amazon says doing that work locally gives it a faster way to get packages to homes and businesses around San Juan.
The roughly two-day estimate applies to the San Juan metro area. Amazon’s announcement leaves open which ZIP codes qualify for faster delivery and how many packages the station can handle each day.
Six delivery companies operate from the site
The six companies are part of Amazon’s Delivery Service Partner program. They pick up packages at the Dorado station and handle the final leg to the customer. Under the program, the delivery companies hire and manage their own drivers, while Amazon provides technology that plans routes based on factors such as package volume and delivery addresses.
Early estimates put the number of driving jobs at about 200 when plans for the station were reported in 2024. Amazon put that figure at about 300 at the formal opening. The estimated number of jobs inside the station was about 100 in 2024, close to the staffing level Amazon reported in November.

Cheapest Corvette ZR-1 Is a Genuine 104k-Mile Barn Find, Gets First Wash in Ages, Revival Isn't Easy
36 photos
Photo: YouTube/Romans 1:16 Garage
Finding a Picasso in the attic would probably be a good day – provided the piece was not reported stolen; the automotive equivalent is unearthing a neglected 1991 Chevrolet Corvette ZR-1 inside a dusty Texas pole barn for the price of a clapped-out Saturn. Of course, you can’t hang a ZR-1 on a wall in the living room, but have you tried adjusting valves on a Picasso? Besides, you can’t wash a Picasso more than once. Which can’t be said about this barn find icon from the 90s.
Documented by the YouTube channel Romans 1:16 Garage, this Bright Red survivor spent 10 years marinating in agricultural obscurity after logging over 104,000 miles as a real-world street machine rather than a climate-controlled museum piece. It’s a bitter-sweet feeling about this car: on one hand, someone obviously enjoyed it to the fullest (104k miles in 25 years is good fun). On the other, the car was abruptly discarded and shoved in the back of the “ I’ll get to it one day ” chest.
According to the seller's lore shared by the YouTuber, the sports car served as a daily driver during its final four years on the asphalt before a failed power steering pump banished it to the farm. When hauled onto a flatbed tow truck, it wore a decade of barn grime, mud splashes, and pine needles, yet miraculously escaped the rodent apocalypse that usually turns dormant classics into five-star mouse hotels.
Beneath the filth, the C4 wore mostly original paint, corroded sawblade alloy wheels, Gorilla Tape sealing a leaky roof edge, and a front bumper cover suffering from a missing air dam corner and giant paint bubbles. Remarkably, its rare factory solar-control Iridium windshield survived intact, casting an iridescent purple-gold glow worthy of Robocop's visor, though explaining that factory tint to a skeptical Texas state trooper promises future comedy.
Photo: YouTube/Romans 1:16 Garage Opening the doors revealed a cockpit that looked like Marty McFly left the T-tops off in Death Valley. Ten years of brutal Texas heat baked the red leather sport seats into cracked, torn jerky and bleached the once-crimson carpets into faded pumpkin fuzz. Aside from loose console change toward the repair bill, the radio and climate controls were dead, though the dash pad and six-speed shifter survived.
Reviving this sleeping giant required triage before glamour. Finding uncontaminated oil and coolant, the wrencher scrubbed the grime, installed a fresh battery, spark plugs, dual fuel pumps, filters, and socks, and coaxed the dormant V8 back to life. A subsequent full detail and wax restored the paint's luster and blackened the under-hood trim, turning a barn casualty into a running, stopping, respectable driver.
Still, turning a $100-per-wheel curbed survivor into a sorted cruiser remains a projected year-long marathon. While the engine runs strong and the brakes bite, peeling front brake lines mean all four corners need fresh soft hoses, and the bubbled front bumper demands a respray. Fortunately, replacement weather stripping, carpet kits, leather seat skins, a shift knob, and a boot are already inbound to erase the cabin's sunstroke.
Photo: YouTube/Romans 1:16 Garage To appreciate why rescuing a beat-up 1991 ZR-1 is such a big deal, rewind to 1970, when General Motors quietly slipped Regular Production Option ZR1 onto the third-generation Corvette order sheet. Unadvertised and built for hardcore road racers , that original C3 package paired a 370-horsepower solid-lifter 350-cubic-inch LT1 V8 with a Muncie 4-speed manual, stiff suspension, and zero radio, air conditioning, or power windows.
Across eight Corvette generations, only five have worn the sacred ZR1 badge: C3, C4, C6, C7, and C8. Chevrolet built 53 C3 units from 1970 to 1972, 6,939 C4 models from 1990 to 1995, 4,684 examples in the C6 series from 2009 to 2013, and 2,953 C7 coupes and convertibles in 2019. Adding 1,824 C8 ZR1s and 318 hybrid ZR1X units built so far brings total production to 16,771.
After emissions rules turned late-1970s Corvettes into lethargic disco cruisers, the 1990 C4 ZR-1 arrived like Arnold Schwarzenegger crashing a kindergarten party. Dubbed “King of the Hill” by Chevrolet engineers, it shattered the stereotype that American sports cars only excelled at drag strips, humiliating contemporary Ferrari 348 and Porsche 911 Turbo exotics in braking, cornering, and endurance reliability while reestablishing Corvette as a world-class nameplate.
Photo: YouTube/Romans 1:16 Garage Under its clamshell hood sat a revolutionary 5.7-liter, 350-cubic-inch V8. Before you say “what’s revolutionary about an SBC?”, remember the engine had only the displacement in common with the regular motors from regular Corvettes. The all-aluminum LT5 in the ZR-1 was designed with Lotus and hand-assembled by speedboat builder Mercury Marine.
Ditching traditional pushrods for four overhead camshafts actuating 32 valves, and a three-stage 16-runner intake governed by a dashboard valet key, it made 375 horsepower and 370 lb-ft of torque (380 PS / 502 Nm) from 1990 to 1992, before upgrades bumped output to 405 horsepower and 385 lb-ft (410 PS, 522 Nm) from 1993 through 1995.
Chevrolet bolted that exotic V8 to a stout German ZF 6-speed manual transmission, Bilstein FX3 electronic selective ride dampers, 13-inch front brakes, and massive 315/35ZR17 Goodyear rear tires tucked beneath a rear body widened by three inches. The payoff was volcanic: 0 to 60 mph in 4.4 seconds, the quick-quarter dash in 12.8 seconds at 111 mph (179 kph), a 179-mph top speed (288 kph), and 24-hour world endurance records.
Photo: YouTube/Romans 1:16 Garage Superpower status carried eye-watering sticker shock that made buyers feel like Gordon Gekko signing a leveraged buyout (if the name doesn’t sound familiar in the slightest, I invite you to watch “Wall Street,” the 1987 movie starring Michael Douglas). In 1990, the ZR-1 package added $27,016 to the $31,979 base coupe for a $58,995 total, rising in 1991 to $31,683 atop a $32,455 coupe for a grand total of $64,138. One could simply buy two Corvettes for the price of a ZR-1.
Meanwhile, the second-most performant factory options, the $460 Z51 or $2,155 Z07 packages on the 245-horsepower L98, cost pennies, leaving only the $33,000 Callaway B2K Twin Turbo in that financial stratosphere.
This classic ZR-1 is one of just 2,044 units built in 1991, and it proves that legends never die; they just nap in a Texas pole barn until someone with a wrench and a sense of humor shows up. Even with 104,000 miles and a sun-scorched cabin, this resurrected King of the Hill packs more presence than a whole dealership lot of modern appliances.

By Charlotte Goldstone
17 November 2026
Warehouse operators are ramping up investment in artificial intelligence and automation, despite continuing difficulties proving the financial benefits, according to new research published today.
A study by MIT’s Intelligent Logistics Systems Lab and warehouse technology provider Mecalux found that 90% of companies expect to increase spending on generative and agentic AI over the next two to three years.
The MIT–Mecalux research, involving 1,967 supply chain and warehousing professionals across 21 countries, found 83% had already reported accelerating AI adoption in the past year.
However, although 87% of generative AI applications and 81% of agentic AI applications reportedly delivered at least moderate operational improvements, only 39% and 36%, respectively, achieved significant gains that could be supported by documented figures.
Around three in ten formal return-on-investment assessments were inconclusive or below expectations, according to the research.
The study also found that 40% of organisations had abandoned at least one AI initiative over the past two years – integration difficulties, poor data quality, and disappointing returns among the principal reasons.
The findings come as major logistics operators GXO and Ceva unveiled ambitious plans to expand the use of robotics and AI in their warehouse operations.
Ceva Logistics today announced a five-year collaboration with the Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) to establish the Intelligent Logistics & Autonomous Systems Lab, supported by the Singapore Economic Development Board and National Robotics Programme.
It will focus on automating labour-intensive, high-mix, low-volume value-added services (VAS), including kitting, labelling, and packing, using robotics, AI vision systems, and connected automation.
Ceva said VAS accounted for approximately half the warehouse floor hours at its automated Blue Hub facility in Singapore, where solutions developed through the lab are expected to be deployed within one to two years.
Guy Meredith, Ceva’s contract logistics VP, APAC, said: “Our ambition is to build on validated solutions for new applications across customer sectors and our Asia Pacific network, using lessons from each deployment to shape further innovation.”
Meanwhile, during GXO Logistics’ Investor Day yesterday, the company outlined automation-led growth targets to 2030 of annual organic revenue growth exceeding 7%, and an adjusted EBITA margin above 6.5%.
According to the presentation, approximately 40% of GXO’s operations are already automated, compared with its estimate of an industry average of 15% to 20%.
The company said it expected automation, warehouse AI, and adaptive technology to generate an additional $50m–$70m in annual EBITA run-rate savings over the four-year plan.
GXO also identified Asia-Pacific, Mexico, and Central and Eastern Europe as expansion opportunities, although its presentation did not specify funded warehouse projects across those markets.
Last week, GXO announced a letter of intent with robotics developer Apptronik to expand trials of Apollo humanoid robots, potentially deploying up to 1,000 units over four years. The proposal remains conditional on further development and successful trials, rather than representing a confirmed purchase commitment.
The MIT–Mecalux study found that 57% of respondents expected AI to execute more than 25% of warehouse operational decisions autonomously by 2028.
Inevitably this highlighted human workforce implications, with 56% reporting that AI had shifted employees towards higher-value tasks, while 11% reported headcount reductions.

Black Friday Bangers: Here Are Five Brands With Some Wild Sales on Their "Death Machines"
21 photos
Photo: Autoevolution | Florin Profir
Over the past couple of years, there has been an explosion in one particular vehicle. It’s not the car, or the bicycle, but rather, the e-scooter. This mobility solution has gained massive traction and with good reasons: they’re nimble, easy to use, and often, pretty darned affordable. Well, with Black Friday sales lighting up all around the world, that “affordable” is about to transform into a “steal.”
Ah, the good old Black Friday, an event that people look forward to time and time again and year after year, and who can blame us: it can be the best time to snag that something you’ve always wanted and at a price that you won’t see again until next year, if ever.
Well, e-scooter brands are also hopping in on the action , slashing prices on some of their most significant machines, and that’s what we’re here to explore. I’ve chosen five of my favorite brands that are currently slashing prices on their beasts, marking it as the perfect time to leave your car at home, if only for a few tasks each day.
Ausom First up on our list of brands that are really hitting the Black Friday sauce is none other than Ausom, a brand whose lineup I have literally decimated in my tests and a brand that simply hits the sweet spot in so many ways, not to mention giving the market what it wants.
Photo: Ausom Ausom is really dropping prices off on their e-scooters, with tried and tested beasts like the DT2 Pro going for as little as $1,100, and the L2 Max Dual Motor and GoSoul 2 Pro, flying off the shelf for a reduced $850.
Keep in mind that the SR1 and F1 Max are also seeing price cuts, e-scooters that I haven’t had the pleasure of testing just yet because when Ausom has then in stock, they’re gone instantly! They too are seeing price cuts of at least $100.
Segway Up next, we have the one and only Segway, a brand that the entire world has heard of . They to are dropping rates quite drastically, with the Max G3 Plus selling for $300 less, or $1,200. Other, entry-level machines, like the F3, is selling for $650, down from a flat $1,000.
Photo: Segway But, there may be no deal better in the Segway aisles, so to speak, than the Max G2, selling for a massively reduced price of $630, down from $1,400. This is the best deal in Segway’s lineup.
Still, not all Segway scooters are up for grabs at lower prices. The latest GT3 Pro SuperScooter is seeing no price cuts, flying off the shelf for $2,700, still. Keep in mind that this is also one of the best-rated e-scooters from the brand, so there are clear reasons why Segway chose to not lower the price.
NanRobot As we move forward with the Black Friday deals, we arrive at NanRobot, a crew that, while it may not be as well-known as Segway or even Ausom, is right up there as one of those brands that kicks out hyper-scooters, insanely fast and powerful machines that we can call upon to actually fly around at speeds as fast as your car.
Their performance lineup of e-scooters is seeing some major price cuts because of Black Friday, with the LS7+ selling for $2,400, reduced $600. It’s their fastest and most expensive e-scooter, capable of reaching 74.5 mph and cranking out a peak of 81 miles of ride time.
Photo: NANROBOT If that’s too much power, check out the X8, going for $389 and limited to just 18 miles of speed but with a range of 25 miles on a full charge.
Now, NanBot also has a simple commuter lineup, with e-scooters now selling for as low as $300, down from $520, so if this is not the time to check in with these brands, I don’t know when is.
Niu Also on this list of essential e-scooter brands to consider for this year’s Black Friday sales includes none other than Niu. This is one of those crews that has always been there in the background, selling their e-scooters all incognito like, but enough to ensure they stay alive, and they have been going strong for several years now.
Photo: NIU Niu prepares their lineup with e-scooters that are even selling for $1,000 their starting price. The carbon fiber KQi Air X is that unit, going for just $1,050, down from $1,900. Another considerable deal is the KQi 300X, one of this crew’s AT rides, and also selling for just $800, down from $1,400. Prices on others are also slashed, so be sure to dive in deeper into their lineup.
Pure Electric Now, the last beast on our list is a team that I don’t expect you to have heard of. Pure Electric is that brand, the one and the same started off by Adam Norris and McLaren. Yes, McLaren can be spotted on an e-scooter, and the Pure x McLaren Flex is selling for £200 less than it was before, going for just £900. The standard Pure Flex is selling for £875 ($1,150), in case you don’t care if it say McLaren on the side of your ride.
Photo: Pure x McLaren Their most affordable option, on the other hand, is the Escape, selling for just £350 ($461), down from £430.
Oh, and pricing for Pure can be found in British Pounds as they’re for sale over in the UK and Europe. Keep in mind, however, that Pure is setting its sights on the US market too. You can start saving up your cash now that you know this.
While these are not the only e-scooter brands out there that are pulling the trigger on amazing deals, they are some of the one’s you should consider. If you have any other brands you’re a big fan of, drop a comment in the section below; it’ll help other readers too.

Sellas Life Sciences’ investigational cancer vaccine prolonged median overall survival by over nine months compared to standard of care in a Phase 3 trial for difficult-to-treat acute myeloid leukemia.
Sellas Life Sciences is gearing up for an FDA submission after its off-the-shelf cancer vaccine slashed the risk of death by 41% for patients with acute myeloid leukemia.
The Phase 3 REGAL trial enrolled 126 patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML), a cancer that starts in the bone marrow and quickly spreads to the blood. Patients were in their second or later remission or were in remission and ineligible for an allogeneic stem cell transplant.
The randomized, open-label study tested Sellas’ immunotherapeutic cancer vaccine, called galinpepimut-S (GPS), as a maintenance monotherapy designed to extend survival. The experimental treatment was tied to a median overall survival of 24 months compared to 14.7 months for patients receiving an investigator’s choice of the best available treatment. The findings translate to a statistically significant death risk reduction of 41%, hitting the study’s main goal.
Based on the findings, Sellas is preparing to meet with the FDA about a potential accelerated pathway and approval submission in the first half of next year, according to a Tuesday release .
“Given the significant unmet need in this patient population, we look forward to engaging with the FDA to discuss the results and the regulatory path forward, with the goal of making this therapy available to patients as rapidly as possible,” Sellas CEO Angelos Stergiou said in the press release.
GPS was generally well tolerated, with treatment-related adverse events “predominantly mild to moderate” and most commonly consisting of local injection site reactions, according to Sellas.
The New York biotech is currently conducting a statistical evaluation of REGAL’s secondary endpoints and plans to share detailed findings at an upcoming medical conference.

“Patients with AML in second remission who cannot undergo allogeneic stem cell transplantation face poor survival outcomes and have a significant need for new treatment approaches,” members of the REGAL study steering committee said in a joint statement.
“The landmark data from the Phase 3 REGAL trial demonstrate a statistically significant and clinically meaningful overall survival advantage for the GPS immunotherapeutic cancer vaccine in this underserved population. By training the immune system to target residual leukemia cells, GPS addresses a critical unmet need and has the potential to redefine the treatment paradigm in AML maintenance therapy.”
Designed at Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center lab, GPS consists of four WT1-derived peptides. The vaccine candidate is made to stimulate both CD4+ and CD8+ T cell immune responses against WT1-expressing cancer cells.
REGAL is Sella’s most advanced trial, though the biotech has tested GPS in smaller, earlier studies for ovarian cancer and mesothelioma. The company also touts a CDK9 inhibitor candidate, called SLS009 or tambiciclib, in testing for different cancers, including AML.

BMW Assembles Just Around 70 Units of the iX5 Daily at the Spartanburg Plant in the US
10 photos
Photo: BMW
BMW is building approximately 70 examples of the brand-new iX5 every single day at its Spartanburg complex in South Carolina, and the iX5 also happens to be the German automaker's first US-assembled electric vehicle. The Munich-based manufacturer obviously has bigger plans for the factory, with BMW intending to assemble no fewer than six zero-emission models stateside by 2030.
Even though BMW hasn't formally identified the remaining five models, we do know that both the iX6 and iX7 are in the offing. The San Luis Potosi facility in Mexico will handle the bulk of North American-market Neue Klasse production, beginning with the iX3 sport utility vehicle and the i3 sedan. The iX4, meanwhile, is exclusively produced at the EV-centric Debrecen plant in Hungary.
As reported by Automotive News, the German automaker has invested a tremendous $1.7 billion in the South Carolina operations to expand the Spartanburg plant while also building a new battery-making complex in nearby Woodruff. The cited publication reports that suppliers have been informed of a 60,000-vehicle output in 2027, down from an earlier forecast of 100,000.
It should get better, though. BMW told suppliers that 175,000 electric vehicles may be produced at Spartanburg annually in 2028 and 2029, although said estimate is understandably subject to change.
As good an estimate as a manufacturer can come up with based on current data, consumer demand can change overnight. As such, it would be foolish to expect BMW of North America to successfully hit its 175,000-vehicle targets in 2028 and 2029.
In any case, the iX5 is a very important battery-electric vehicle for the Bavarian company. The US-market 60 xDrive uses two electric motors and sixth-generation battery tech, with BMW of North America claiming 570 horsepower and 593 pound-feet (804 Newton-meters) of twist in optimal conditions.
Photo: BMW Maximum driving range? Depending on optional equipment, look forward to anything from 418 to 456 miles (673 to 734 kilometers) on a full charge of its absolutely massive high-voltage battery. Listed with 144 kilowatt-hours of net energy, the Gen6 battery delivers 20 percent greater energy density than the older prismatic cells that BMW uses in the 2026 model year iX.
Good for 4.4 seconds to 60 miles per hour (97 kilometers per hour) and no more than 130 miles per hour (210 kilometers per hour) when equipped with the right tires, the iX5 is an 800-volt affair that benefits from cell-to-pack structural integration to boost energy density and chassis rigidity. The CTP route cuts manufacturing costs, but it also introduces higher pack-level repair complexity.
The cell-to-pack method is harder to justify when a single cell goes bad. The problem here is that cell-to-pack layouts bond the cells directly into the enclosure, making it extremely hard to replace a bad cell. Because the cell-to-pack housing is a load-bearing part of the underbody structure, collisions obviously carry a higher risk of compromising the battery and structural integrity.
Plant Woodruff is tasked with building Gen6 batteries for the iX5 , but alas, there is a transition period in the supply chain that must be highlighted. Initial cells will be imported from China before switching to South Korean cells from an Arizona plant toward the end of the decade. This move will end BMW of North America's partnership with AESC, which builds the iX5's cells in China.

Quirky T-19A Kestrel Beats the B-21 Raider Nuclear Bomber in Becoming USAF's Newest Airplane
7 photos
Photo: USAF
In the military world, new aircraft types don't come along very often. Sure, you could argue that new planes are revealed all the time, but that mostly happens because much older platforms are being modernized and upgraded to fulfil new roles. When it comes to an aircraft type that hasn't been used before, as said, they don't come along very often.
When it comes to the American Air Force , the eyes of the world are affixed to the upcoming B-21 Raider nuclear bomber and the F-47 sixth-generation fighter, but those are still a long way from being ready to join the fleet as the newest aircraft around. Until that happens, a new kind of airplane entered the scene.
They call it the T-19A Kestrel, the work of Arkansas-based Game Aerospace, and it has been created with a specific goal in mind: to serve the needs of the U.S. Air Force Academy by training some of its pilots in the art of aerobatics.
That's right, aerobatics, because the Academy is now actively pursuing the creation of a national aerobatic and demonstration team. It needs that not only to wow the crowds, but also to get greater cadet involvement in training, demonstrations, and program operations.
The Kestrel, named so in honor of the small predatory bird of the falcon family, is based on the GB1 GameBird, an aerobatic aircraft that first flew a little more than a decade ago, adapted for the use of the Air Force in just ten months of work.
The plane is a tandem-seater, but as small as you'd expect: it only stands 25 feet (7.7 meters) from wing tip to wing tip, and 23 feet (seven meters) from nose to tail. Powering it is a Lycoming six-cylinder piston engine rated at 303 horsepower, which is enough to give it a top speed of 230 mph (370 kph).
The plane officially entered service with the Academy at the end of last week, when the Kestrel debuted as part of a flyover of the Cadet Wing’s noon meal formation. For all intents and purposes, this is the first powered aerobatic aircraft fielded by the Academy.
The organization had four of these things built, and it will use them to give cadets more flight time and aerobatic experience as they seek to enter the Air Force or Undergraduate Pilot Training.
Getting to it using these machines will be six active-duty military pilots from the Academy staff, who, together with the 306th Flying Training Group, will form the initial cadre. These pilots have been tasked with creating and executing an aerobatic training curriculum.
For the moment, these six will also become the primary demonstration pilots, whom we'll probably see soon enough at recruiting events and air shows across the nation.

Marrow Therapeutics aims to address safety and accessibility obstacles in genetic medicines by delivering therapies straight to bone marrow cells.
Marrow Therapeutics is unveiling with $173 million in combined series A and B cash to fuel its efforts to create new and improved treatments for serious blood disorders.
The biotech’s $53 million series A financing was co-led by founder Scion Life Sciences and venBio, according to a Tuesday press release. The remaining $120 million came from a series B led by OrbiMed.
The Watertown, Massachusetts-based biotech will use the new funds to bolster its bone marrow-targeted platform to treat severe blood disorders. The Transferrin Antibody Bioconjugate (TAB) technology aims to deliver therapeutic payloads directly to bone marrow cells to overcome limitations of traditional genetic medicines, such as safety, manufacturing and accessibility concerns.
The biotech is hoping to use its in vivo approach and “pipeline in a product” strategy to more safely and effectively treat conditions such as sickle cell disease (SCD) and beta thalassemia. Marrow’s lead candidate, coded MAR-101, is currently in preclinical studies to enable in-human testing. The asset is designed to treat both SCD and beta thalassemia by reducing the protein-coding gene BCL11a and reactivating fetal hemoglobin production.
Vertex Pharmaceuticals and CRISPR Therapeutics’ Casgevy and Genetix Biotherapeutics’ (formerly bluebird bio) Lyfgenia gained landmark approvals for SCD in December 2023, validating genetic modification as a successful approach to treat the disease. A month later, Casgevy was cleared to treat beta thalassemia, too.
However, both ex vivo therapies demand an intensive administration process and Lyfgenia carries a boxed warning for hematologic cancers, with lifelong monitoring recommended.
“We’re at a pivotal moment in genetic medicine and its application in severe blood disorders—the field has validated key targets and shown that genetic approaches can work, but we need to solve the safety and accessibility challenges to truly transform patient outcomes,” Marrow CEO Romesh Subramanian said in a prepared statement. Subramanian has more than 20 years of industry experience under his belt and is also a venture partner with Scion Life Sciences.
“By precisely targeting the bone marrow, we’re able to deliver the potential of genetic medicines and provide sustained benefit, while simultaneously avoiding the risks that have constrained earlier approaches,” he added.
Subramanian is joined by Chief Scientific Officer Tim Weeden, formerly of Dyne Therapeutics, and Chief Operating and Technology Officer John Najim, also from neuromuscular disease-focused Dyne.

By Gavin van Marle
17 November 2026
Gemini Cooperation partners Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd will have made a full resumption of Suez transits on their Asia-Europe services by mid-January.
Yesterday, the partners outlined the schedule for the last three Asia-North Europe services still detouring via the Cape of Good Hope to return to the Red Sea routing.
The Asia-Northern Europe Loop 1 (Maersk AE2/Hapag-Lloyd NE1) will resume Suez transits in both directions with the departure of the 18,300 teu Mary Maersk from Ningbo on 4 December.
Currently the vessel is returning to Asia having just completed a southbound Suez transit, according to AIS data.
The new pro forma port rotation will be Ningbo-Shanghai-Tanjung Pelepas-Suez Canal-Rotterdam-Wilhelmshaven-Bremerhaven-Rotterdam-Suez Canal-Salalah-Singapore-Ningbo, while according to Xeneta’s eeSea liner database, the switch in routing will see the number of ships on the string reduced from 14 to 13.
The Asia-Northern Europe Loop 3 (Maersk AE3/Hapag-Lloyd NE3) will also fully resume westbound Suez transits following the departure of the 16,300 teu Alette Maersk from Shanghai on 20 December.
That switch will see the number of ships deployed reduced from 13 to 11, and feature the following port rotation: Shanghai-Yantian-Tanjung Pelepas-Suez Canal-London-Gothenburg-Aarhus-Rotterdam-Southampton-Suez Canal-Singapore-Shanghai.
Meanwhile, shippers on the Asia-Northern Europe Loop 2 (Maersk AE1/Hapag-Lloyd NE2), operated entirely by Hagag-Lloyd vessels, will have to wait until early 2027, with a full westbound resumption beginning with the departure of the 23,700 teu Damietta Express from Shanghai on 14 January, representing the last of Gemini’s Asia-Europe strings to return to Suez.
The vessel is currently steaming northbound along the west coast of Africa on its final Cape routing before reverting to the new pro forma rotation, which will be: Shanghai-Yantian-Tanjung Pelepas-Suez Canal-Rotterdam-Hamburg-Antwerp-London-Tangier-Suez Canal-Singapore-Shanghai.
“The Suez Canal is a vital maritime corridor between east and west, and a key driver of efficient global supply chains,” Maersk said in a customer advisory. “The route through the Suez Canal and Red Sea is the fastest, most sustainable, and most efficient way to serve customers with transport between Asia, Europe and the Middle East.
“By transitioning the AE1, AE2, and AE3 to the trans-Suez corridor instead of sailing around the Cape of Good Hope, we will offer more efficient transit times for customers,” it said, adding that it would continue to monitor the security situation in the region, which remains in a state of considerable flux.
It also remains to be seen how the widespread return to Suez routings will impact Asia-Europe schedule reliability, which according to Xeneta data, has fallen to historic lows – just 4% of vessels arrived on time in Europe ex-Asia in September, which rose to 7% in October.
Xeneta data also revealed that nearly 600,000 teu of capacity that had previously been tied up in Cape of Good Hope deployments has already been “released” by Suez returns, and chief analyst Peter Sand predicted this could result in a steep drop in freight rates next year.
“The Red Sea is pivotal to ocean container shipping in 2027 because it offers both sides of the coin,” he told delegates at Xeneta’s annual summit in Munich last week. “If there is a full return, freight rates could plummet.
“We could also be faced with the opposite extreme if a deterioration in the security situation in the Red Sea forces carriers to revert to Cape of Good Hope diversions.
“This would bring chaos to ocean networks and upward pressure on rates.”
And he added: “The significant ramping up of Red Sea services in recent months should not distract from the fragility of the geo-political situation in the wider Middle East – it will not take much to ignite the situation again and then the house of cards comes falling down.”

By Alex Lennane
17 November 2026
Korean Air is maximising its Asia-Americas cargo capacity, as year-round demand for AI infrastructure overlaps traditional peak-season shipments, keeping the pressure on transpacific space even as global weekly volumes soften.
Jaedong Eum, EVP and head of the carrier’s Cargo Business division, told The Loadstar data-centre expansion had become a primary growth engine for the business.
“Entering the traditional November peak season, we are experiencing compounded capacity pressure on the transpacific, driven by overlapping traditional Q4 consumer goods shipments and robust year-round AI-related hardware demand,” he said.
“Consequently, we are maximising our Asia-to-Americas capacity.”
Europe-bound capacity was less constrained, he added, following a moderation in cross-border ecommerce growth.
The airline was seeking Europe-Asia cargo to improve directional balance, while adjusting its US routes and focusing on yields to manage uneven flows.
Korean Air Cargo prioritises its freighters for outsized, heavy, and specialist project shipments, including AI infrastructure, while deploying passenger belly capacity for ecommerce and express parcels.
Its experience illustrates the increasingly uneven airfreight market. Demand for particular commodities and routes is sustaining capacity pressure, despite limited evidence of a broader peak-season acceleration.
WorldACD’s latest figures, published yesterday, show worldwide average prices rose 2% week on week, to $3.45/kg during 2-8 November, up 31% year on year. Chargeable weight fell 2%, while capacity remained flat.
It attributed rising prices to tight capacity, seasonal passenger aircraft redeployment, and maintenance, adding that an anticipated peak-season surge had yet to materialise.
Taiwan bucked the regional decline. Its US-bound tonnage increased 7% week on week, and 37% year on year, which WorldACD attributed to AI-related exports. Across Asia Pacific, US-bound volumes fell 3% over the week, while prices rose 1%.
Forwarders are also reporting technology-driven growth. Expeditors said in its 3 November results that Q3 air tonnage had increased approximately 13% year on year, with South Asia exports particularly strong. Demand from hyperscalers and their suppliers supporting AI infrastructure was a significant contributor, while limited fleet expansion and aircraft delivery delays constrained capacity.
However, next year could bring some rate relief.
Xeneta forecasts global airline average rates will fall Between 5% and 10%, mainly in the second half, as Gulf capacity returns and fuel costs ease. Its base case puts demand growth at 2%-4%, against capacity growth of 3%-5%.
That outlook depends on an early, lasting Gulf peace agreement – without a recovery, it expects rates to remain close to 2026 levels.
Asia Pacific-North America is likely to retain more of its premium because of AI demand, while Asia-Europe shippers should gain negotiating room. A continued return of ocean services through Suez could also draw less time-sensitive shipments back to sea.
Korean Air, nevertheless, expects the underlying technology demand to endure.
“We do not view this as a cyclical peak,” said Mr Eum, describing AI chips and data-centre construction as a structural, long-term investment cycle.
DHL Global Forwarding’s airfreight head, Henk Venema, also expects pressure to persist on selected Asian export routes, particularly Vietnam, Thailand, and Taiwan to the US.
In DHL’s 2027 outlook, he warned that additional passenger flights would not necessarily provide capacity on the routes where it was needed, or accommodate cargo requiring freighters. Lightly loaded return sectors also leave Asian exports carrying more of the round-trip operating cost.
Carriers are responding with new services. FedEx announced four additional weekly China-US 777F flights on 9 November, alongside a five-times-weekly China–Dallas-Fort Worth connection via Anchorage, targeting semiconductors, servers, and AI infrastructure among other sectors.
Pressure also extends to the Indian subcontinent. India-based Ligi Logistics reported very tight US and Canada capacity in its Week 47 advisory, particularly for larger and urgent shipments, alongside controlled allocations and premium rates on selected Europe and UK services.
DHL GF yesterday announced a twice-weekly Hong Kong–Navi Mumbai–Liège 747F service, its first dedicated flight serving India. It initially targets 25–30 tonnes per flight for the India sectors, or 50–60 tonnes weekly. A Bengaluru–Europe service is planned for March.
Meanwhile, airlines are also broadening access through closer network integration.
Qatar Airways Cargo, IAG Cargo, and MASkargo today announced single-booking access to more than 300 destinations across 60 countries under their Global Cargo Joint Business, with more than 400 destinations ultimately planned.
The partnership coordinates capacity, handling, and connections across their networks. MASkargo CEO Mark Jason Thomas said aligning these processes would translate into “greater routing flexibility, smoother connections, and more consistent service for our customers”.
IAG’s experience illustrates the consequences of losing access to freighter capacity. Its third-quarter cargo traffic fell 13.9%, which the group attributed partly to cancelled third-party long-haul freighter capacity, particularly affecting Asia-Pacific, although revenue increased 3.9%.
An IAG Cargo spokesperson told The Loadstar the carrier had changed its third-party freighter capacity this year as it optimised its network, while adding belly capacity and strengthening partner connections.
The joint business provided “additional flexibility and routing options for customers rather than acting as a like-for-like replacement for individual services”, the spokesperson said.

Minister Julio Moltó (left) talks to Cobre Panama mine employees. ( Image courtesy of Ministry of Commerce and Industries. )
Posted By: Cecilia Jamasmie November 17, 2026
Panama has authorized formal negotiations with First Quantum Minerals (TSX: FM) over a potential restart of mining at Cobre Panamá, advancing efforts to resolve a dispute that halted extraction at the copper operation three years ago.
An interministerial team led by Commerce and Industries Minister Julio Moltó will negotiate with the Canadian miner’s local subsidiary, Minera Panamá. Discussions will cover employment, economic benefits, environmental oversight and the termination of arbitration proceedings against the country, President José Raúl Mulino announced Monday.
“We are unclear when and if any of Panama’s negotiating position (fiscal/legal frameworks) will be released but see the commencement of negotiations as a key and positive step to enable a restart of mining operations before broken rock stockpiles run out,” BMO mining analyst Matthew Murphy wrote in a note Tuesday.
The talks could restore extraction at an operation that produced about 331,000 tonnes of copper in 2023. Cobre Panamá is already processing previously mined material under a separate authorization, but those stockpiles are expected to last only until mid-2027. A new agreement would be needed for a broader restart.
Terms of return
First Quantum shares rose. 7.4% to $32.093 on Tuesday morning in Toronto after they closed 7.6% weaker at $29.81 on Monday before Mulino’s announcement, giving it a market value of about $26.7 billion. The stock has traded between $27.68 and $49.27 over the past year. BMO rates the shares outperform with a $60 target.
Mulino outlined five principles governing negotiations: Panamanian ownership of mineral resources, maximum economic benefits for the country, national sovereignty, strict environmental protection and compliance with the constitution and national laws.
Any agreement must include an orderly, verifiable and definitive closure plan financed by the company, with reforestation and measures to prevent environmental damage. Closure would be mandatory, with no possibility of an extension, the presidency said.
Mulino said an agreement would not constitute a mining concession. The government would determine the legal structure for any deal, while public participation, including consultation with nearby communities, would accompany negotiations. No restart date or operating term has been announced.
First Quantum welcomed the announcement Tuesday and said public participation would take place alongside the talks and before any agreement is reached. A restart could create 6,000 direct and 30,000 indirect jobs and business opportunities for about 2,000 registered suppliers, it estimated.
Stockpiles already processing
Mining has been suspended at the site, about 120 km west of Panama City, since November 2023, when Panama’s Supreme Court ruled its operating contract unconstitutional following nationwide protests.
Stockpile processing began in the second quarter of this year. First Quantum expects it to yield 30,000–40,000 tonnes of copper in 2026, with the remaining material processed into next year, the company said in October.
SGS delivered its government-commissioned audit on June 19. The review produced a weighted overall compliance score of 88%, while identifying shortcomings in flora protection, ecological restoration and reforestation, Panama’s government said. The findings did not authorize a restart.
A government commission recommended negotiations on Sept. 30 to assess a new agreement that would settle arbitration claims and allow operations to finance an orderly closure without cost to the state. Most of Monday’s conditions had already been disclosed, Murphy said.
“Most of the requirements stated by the President have been named in previous disclosures,” Murphy wrote. “The statement that the mine life cannot be extended was included in the high-level commission report.”

Aston Martin Brings the CoD: Modern Warfare 4 Dreadnought Into the Real World, To Race It in Dakar
6 photos
Photo: Aston Martin
It rarely happens for a piece of news to keep me on my toes from start to finish, but that's exactly what Aston Martin's latest release managed to do this week. In a nutshell, the more I read, the more my eyes widened and my pulse accelerated, as this is more than a simple piece of news, it's a Christmas gift wrapped like a car.
Its name is Dreadnought , and it was first presented by the British carmaker back in July of this year. It didn't exist in the real world back then, as it was only created digitally to be included in the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 video game.
The digital Dreadnought, created with assistance from video game giants Infinity Ward and Activision, meant a great many things for Aston Martin, the most important of which being that it was its first-ever military-grade tactical SUV.
As such, it comes equipped with things Aston would never dream of fitting on its production cars: integrated weapons storage, adaptive combat zone intelligence systems, reserve fuel tanks, and tactical toggles to be used by players to raise bulletproof shields or call in airstrikes.
The SUV, which is powered by a digital V12 tied to an all-wheel drive system, is fully drivable in the game, and you probably only need to go online to see it in action, proving itself – I wouldn't know, I am actually a Battlefield guy.
{fullimg}
When it was presented a few months ago, nobody dreamed Aston would take the Dreadnought beyond the digital realm and the non-functional model shown at the Fanatics Fest NYC. Yet it is exactly what the carmaker announced this week – the piece of news that really got my blood pumping.
Long story short, the military-spec SUV from CoD will be officially brought into the physical world not to fight wars, but to take on the challenges of the 2027 Dakar race. There will not be a single one of them, but three.
Called just like the video game version, Dreadnought, the SUV does not exist in the real world in completed form yet, but it's getting pretty close, with British engineering crew Prodrive tasked with engineering, building, and racing it in the first couple of weeks of next year, alongside Aston Martin Racing.
All of the above means we don't have the specs of the design yet, but it doesn't mean there aren't more exciting things about it. Like, say, who has been tasked with getting behind the wheel of the Dreadnought and race it to the win, or as close as possible to that.
{fullimg}
As said, there will be three of these cars taking part in the endurance rally next year, and the British carmaker already knows who will be driving them: Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Aramco Formula 1 Team driver and two-time world champion, nine-time FIA World Rally champion Sebastien Loeb , and reigning FIA World Rally Raid champion Lucas Moraes.
Quite the lineup for what is officially Aston Martin Racing's first dive into the world of rally-raid, but despite that, the British crew won't have it easy. The premier prototype class of the competition where it will race will throw at it things made by some of the world's most powerful automotive houses.
It also happens to be one of the most challenging Dakar races in years, as in 2027 we'll be dealing with an entirely new route – a forced move, admittedly, caused by the conflicts in the area, but that won’t stop me from seeing the next Dakar as a breath of fresh air.
The 49th edition of the competition kicks off in Loule, Portugal, on January 9, with the prologue, and will get going a day later with the first special stage, which includes a transfer to the port of embarkation for Nador, Morocco.
{fullimg}
Following a night crossing of the Mediterranean Sea, teams will find themselves on the African continent on January 11, and they'll stand there until the finish, 12 stages and exactly two weeks later.
The 2027 Dakar race is scheduled to end in Marrakech, Morocco, on January 23, following 4,228 miles (6,805) of intense racing, of which 2,697 miles (4,341 km) are special stages.
We will keep an eye on Aston Martin and report back as soon as the Brits reveal more, including the technical details of the Dreadnought desert racer. Until then, you can enjoy it in the photos the carmaker released.
By the looks of it, we're only dealing with renderings of the vehicle, which in some cases appear to depict a Hot Wheels creation rather than a real-world Dakar contender, but that's probably not far from the way the ride will look once ready and presented in its physical form. And we probably don't have much waiting to do until that happens, seeing how the 2027 Dakar is less than two months away from the time of writing.
